newsitem.title: UK: Gold mired near bottom of range, lacks impetus.
newsitem.headline: Gold mired near bottom of range, lacks impetus.

text.p: Gold sulked at weak levels on Tuesday morning in a thin market, weighed down by the threat of more overhead selling.
The origin of a sell-off on Monday, which knocked prices off a peak around $327 per ounce, was the subject of debate, with some targeting central banks as the culprits and others producers.
Spot gold fixed in the morning little changed at $322.10 per ounce, down 50 cents from Monday's afternoon fix.
The fix was well down from the previous morning setting of $326.05 when falls in equities were giving a boost to gold prices.
"I think we could see more selling on any move up to $325 or $326, but decent physical buying is coming in at $321 and $320," a dealer said.
Business was sparse early on Tuesday and prices kept to a tight range between $321.50 and $322.50, basis bids.
Some players suspected the bout of selling on Monday came from another central bank, since short-term lease rates have firmed recently.
The one-month implied lease rate had risen nearly one percentage point over the past week until Monday, but eased by 0.31 point to 2.44 percent on Tuesday.
But others were sceptical and reckoned that producers and speculators were the main sellers, since lease rates have firmed across the board into the forward market, a key focus for miners.
"The longer-term lease rates are also firm...producers have been selling at lower and lower levels this year," a senior dealer said.
The one-year lease rate had not gained as much as the short-term one on the week, but was steady on Tuesday at 2.35 percent.
Speculators who have taken profits from bearish positions when the market approached the $330 area were now borrowing gold to establish fresh shorts, some analysts said.
Selling by producers allowed the shorts to liquidate positions without pushing up prices too much.
Silver was sluggish, straying little from Monday's closing prices just above $4.50 per ounce and keeping in a tiny two-cent range.
The market would find difficulty breaking through resistance around $4.58 after being capped at those levels the two previous days.
"A lot depends on gold. If gold breaks lower, silver will find it difficult to stay up here," a dealer said.
Below the current $4.50-$4.60 range, support was pegged at recent lows around $4.40.
Platinum and palladium were both slightly weaker, apparently hit by reports of more Russian spot sales, dealers said.
But they may be nearing the bottom of the current downtrend, some analysts said.

"Russian selling continues to pressure the PGMs, but there are many traders who feel that $200 for palladium and $400 for platinum may be unofficial floors for the country's exports," broker GNI said in a commentary.
Platinum was indicated at $414.00/$419.00 per ounce, down $1.50, and palladium at $201.00/$206.00 per ounce, off $5.25.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
